motion.name: selector-duet
motion.purpose: Two rhythms on one object: the card lifts 3px/4px while the portrait rises 16px straight up and scales 1.05 from its feet, with no rotation.

motion.name: halftone-blobs
motion.value: 4 drifting blobs (2 on narrow screens), smooth radial falloff, 7-16s life
motion.purpose: One canvas clipped to the cream roster section draws a fine halftone grid where most dots stay at base size; a few soft blobs drift, pulse, fade and respawn to swell dots locally with a gradient edge. One batched fill per frame, paused offscreen and under reduced motion.

narrative.overview: This is a fan-built team hub dressed as a seasonal streetwear lookbook. The team's red is not an accent on a neutral page: it is a garment-dyed ground that owns whole regions, with ink black, warm paper and a single brass tone supporting it. The roster reads as a lineup, player details live on hangtags, and sections are joined by stitched rules rather than generic dividers. The result should feel like opening a collection, not scrolling a sports template. The roster home (index.html) is the reference implementation. Its champions hero, facts rail, off-grid selector rack, record table, history split and shop teaser are the most resolved expressions of this world, and new work should be judged against them first. The site is deliberately unofficial: every page states that it is fan-made, and the shop keeps official and fan-made merchandise visibly apart behind a thin stitched line. Imagery is real team photography and transparent player cutouts from the club's own portrait set; no player likeness is fabricated. Text is set in a condensed display face for names and a workhorse grotesk for everything functional, so hierarchy comes from scale and weight rather than decoration. The other five pages — shop, media, titles, matches and community — share the shell, tokens, footer and baseline grid, but have not received the same depth of refinement as the home page. Their distinct patterns are documented in Components so that nothing unique to them is lost when the home page leads.
keyCharacteristics: Red as ground, not trim; cream paper as the quiet counter-surface.
Hangtags, woven labels, barcode-like strips and stitched dividers as the component vocabulary.
Square corners throughout; no rounded UI chrome.

Three quiet, user-pinned loops: the champions photograph breathes slowly, the facts rail slides continuously, and the roster section's dot field pulses in size like a slow wave; all pause offscreen. The photo, copy and hangtag also sit on pointer-driven depth planes. Everything else is still except immediate hover feedback.
Honest, plainspoken copy that never implies team endorsement.
The roster home leads; the other pages inherit the shell and carry their own documented patterns.
Tab stops are actions: the selector rack reveals one player at a time, and focus is never visually removed.
The primary navigation has four top-level entries with the remaining pages grouped under "More".

rules.name: The Red Ground Rule
rules.body: If a region is red, its text is opaque cream. Tinted cream, muted gray and brass-on-red all fail; the red owns the region and the copy sits on top at full strength.

rules.name: The Eleven-Pixel Floor
rules.body: Nothing functional renders below 11px. The micro-label look comes from tracking and case, not from shrinking type.

rules.name: The Home-First Rule
rules.body: The roster home is the reference surface. When a component or spacing decision is ambiguous, copy what index.html does before inventing a new treatment, and treat the other pages as inheritors until they receive their own attention.

rules.name: The One Reading Path Rule
rules.body: Content text is always left-aligned. Only the punch-hole label on a hangtag and the small flag on a selector card are centred, because they are printed marks on an object rather than page copy.

rules.name: The Edge-First Rule
rules.body: Reach for a border before a shadow. A row of identical hairline-border-plus-wide-shadow cards is the default this world refuses.

rules.name: The Restrained Depth Rule
rules.body: No hard offset shadows. Depth comes from a 2-3px offset and a soft blur; emphasis on selector cards comes from the brass border and red field, not a large coloured block behind the card.

rules.name: The Real Action Rule
rules.body: Nothing is focusable without an action. The selector cards are buttons that reveal one player's detail and toggle it off on a second activation; :focus-visible always keeps a brass outline, including under reduced motion.

rules.name: The True Weight Rule
rules.body: Anton has one real weight. Never let the UA default 700 or font-synthesis invent a bold cut; reset headings to 400. Prose measures stay within 45-70ch and card titles share one 22px role.

rules.name: The Single-Theme Rule
rules.body: The palette is exactly ten hex values, each equal to a declared token, with no dark-mode variant. A pinned single-theme brief is intentional here; a scheme swap would replace the lookbook's material identity. Do not introduce one.

rules.name: The Tap-Target Floor
rules.body: Every inline text link - primary nav, More menu, fan cards, footer links and the credits disclosure - shares one min-height: var(--tap) rule (28px) defined once near the base link styles. Component padding stays local for visual reasons, but the hit-area floor is global. Functional text never drops below 11px.

rules.name: The Pinned Detector Exceptions
rules.body: cramped-padding, marquee and cream-palette are suppressed in .impeccable/config.json because they flag pinned choices, not defects: full-bleed bands inset text via .wrap/--pad, the facts rail is a requested loop paused on hover/focus/offscreen, and --paper/--cream are named tokens with red as the dominant ground.

rules.name: The Halftone Rule
rules.body: The dots are printed texture on the cream paper, not a backdrop effect: they stay inside the section, keep one red at fixed opacity, and most stay at base size. Movement belongs to a few drifting blobs that swell dots locally with a soft edge - never to a uniform per-dot wave or a scaled, sliding field.

dos: Do let red occupy entire regions; do not sprinkle it as a highlight on a white template.
Do use real team photography once per editorial moment; do not invent player portraits or statistics.
Do keep official and fan-made merchandise visibly separate with working outbound links.
Do state "unofficial fan hub" in the header and footer of every page.
Do judge new work against the roster home first, then check the other-page patterns above before inventing a new component.
Do keep every tabbable element actionable and every focus state visible, especially under reduced motion.
donts: Don't add rounded corners, glass blur, gradient text or neon glow.
Don't use Unicode glyphs as icons; draw marks in CSS and hide decorative ones from assistive tech.
Don't scatter entrance animations. The loops are explicit user requests: keep them slow, pause them offscreen and on hover for the rail, and preserve a reduced-motion path.
Don't let any functional text drop below 11px, and never place brass or tinted cream on red copy.
